gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I had already eaten,' she said. She said she ___ already eaten.
gaps.explanation: The past perfect cannot backshift further; it remains had + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'Stop the car!' the passenger shouted. The passenger shouted at the driver ___ the car.
gaps.hint: shout at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The command is reported with shout at + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
gaps.explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Where do you live?' he asked me. He asked me where I ___.
gaps.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, and present simple backshifts: do you live → I lived.
